approvalTitle: URC Engine Parity + Test Suite — Tasks
content:
# Tasks: URC Engine Parity + Comprehensive Test Suite

## Phase A: Extension Schema + Event Timestamp

- [ ] 1. Create URC extensions schema and event timestamp components
  - Files: `ucc/urc_app/schema/urc_extensions_schema.yaml`, `ucc/urc_app/package/lib/urc/components/event_timestamp.py`
  - Define JSON Schema for `CursorBasedTimestamp`, `FieldBasedTimestamp`, `FetchTimestamp`
  - Implement all three as registered components with `resolve(record, config, stream_def) -> float`
  - `CursorBasedTimestamp`: reads `cursor_field` + `datetime_format` from sibling `incremental_sync`
  - `FieldBasedTimestamp`: explicit field/format with Jinja2 interpolation
  - `FetchTimestamp`: returns `time.time()`
  - Handle: string parsing, epoch passthrough (int/float), missing field fallback
  - Purpose: Schema-driven `_time` resolution for Splunk events
  - _Leverage: `urc/registry.py`, `urc/interpolation.py`, `urc/engine.py`_
  - _Requirements: R1, R3_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec 05-urc-engine-parity, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: Python developer with Splunk and schema-driven architecture expertise | Task: Create `urc_extensions_schema.yaml` defining three EventTimestamp component types as JSON Schema, then implement them in `event_timestamp.py` as registered components. Integrate into `engine.py` — after transformations, resolve `_time` via the timestamp component and inject into record before yielding. Default behavior: if no `event_timestamp` block but `incremental_sync` exists, auto-derive (CursorBasedTimestamp). If neither, use FetchTimestamp. All fields support Jinja2 via `eval_string()`. | Restrictions: Do not modify `declarative_component_schema.yaml`. Keep extension schema separate. Register components via `@component()` decorator. | Success: `_time` is present as epoch float in every yielded record. Manifests with no `event_timestamp` block auto-derive from cursor. Explicit config overrides work. Extension schema validates the three types._

- [ ] 2. Integrate event timestamp into engine pipeline
  - File: `ucc/urc_app/package/lib/urc/engine.py`
  - In `_collect_stream()`: after transformations, before yield, resolve `_time`
  - Build timestamp component from `stream_def.get("event_timestamp")` or auto-derive default
  - Pass `stream_def` to resolver so `CursorBasedTimestamp` can read sibling `incremental_sync`
  - Register `event_timestamp` module in `components/__init__.py`
  - Purpose: Wire timestamp resolution into the existing engine pipeline
  - _Leverage: `urc/engine.py`, `urc/components/event_timestamp.py`, `urc/registry.py`_
  - _Requirements: R1, R3_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec 05-urc-engine-parity, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: Python developer | Task: Modify `_collect_stream()` in `engine.py` to build an event timestamp component from `stream_def.get("event_timestamp")`. If absent and `incremental_sync` exists, default to `CursorBasedTimestamp`. If neither, default to `FetchTimestamp`. Call `resolver.resolve(record, config, stream_def)` after transformations, set `record["_time"]`. Add import to `components/__init__.py`. | Restrictions: Do not change the yield signature `(stream_name, record, state)`. Keep `_time` as a field in the record dict. | Success: Every yielded record has `_time` as epoch float. Existing tests still pass._

## Phase B: Engine Gap Components

- [ ] 3. Implement CsvDecoder, JsonlDecoder, ZipfileDecoder
  - File: `ucc/urc_app/package/lib/urc/components/decoders.py`
  - `CsvDecoder`: stdlib `csv.DictReader`, config for `delimiter`, `quotechar`, `encoding`, `skip_rows`. Handle BOM, malformed rows (skip + log warning), empty responses.
  - `JsonlDecoder`: split on newlines, `json.loads()` each line. Skip empty/malformed lines with warning.
  - `ZipfileDecoder`: stdlib `zipfile` + `io.BytesIO`, configurable `inner_decoder` (default JSON). Decode each file in the archive.
  - Purpose: Support CSV, JSONL, ZIP response formats from REST APIs
  - _Leverage: `urc/components/decoders.py` (existing JsonDecoder pattern), `urc/registry.py`_
  - _Requirements: R1_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec 05-urc-engine-parity, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: Python developer | Task: Add `CsvDecoder`, `JsonlDecoder`, `ZipfileDecoder` to `decoders.py` following the existing `JsonDecoder` pattern. Each has `decode(response) -> list[dict]`. CsvDecoder uses stdlib `csv.DictReader` with BOM stripping and malformed row handling. JsonlDecoder splits on newlines. ZipfileDecoder decompresses via `zipfile.ZipFile(BytesIO(response.content))` and decodes each file with a configurable inner decoder. | Restrictions: No external dependencies — stdlib only (csv, zipfile, io, json). Register via `@component()`. | Success: All three decoders handle valid input, edge cases (BOM, empty, malformed), and are registered in the component registry._

- [ ] 4. Implement DpathFlattenFields, KeysReplace, SchemaNormalization transformations
  - File: `ucc/urc_app/package/lib/urc/components/transformations.py`
  - `DpathFlattenFields`: flatten a specific nested field using dpath, config for `field_path` and `delete_origin`
  - `KeysReplace`: find/replace patterns in record keys, config for `replacements` list of `{old, new}` pairs, recursive
  - `SchemaNormalization`: normalize all keys to lowercase + underscores, strip special chars
  - Purpose: Complete the transformation component set for CDK parity
  - _Leverage: `urc/components/transformations.py` (existing patterns), `dpath` library_
  - _Requirements: R1_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec 05-urc-engine-parity, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: Python developer | Task: Add three transformation components to `transformations.py`. `DpathFlattenFields` uses `dpath.util.get()` to extract a nested field, flattens it into the parent with separator, optionally deletes origin. `KeysReplace` iterates `replacements` config applying `str.replace(old, new)` recursively on all dict keys. `SchemaNormalization` lowercases keys, replaces non-alphanumeric with underscore, strips leading/trailing underscores. All follow the existing `transform(record, config, **context) -> dict` interface. | Restrictions: `DpathFlattenFields` may use the `dpath` library (already a dependency). Others use stdlib only. | Success: All three registered, handle nested dicts, empty records, and keys with special characters._

- [ ] 5. Implement CartesianProductStreamSlicer
  - File: `ucc/urc_app/package/lib/urc/components/partition_router.py`
  - Generate cross-product of multiple partition routers via `itertools.product`
  - Config: `stream_slicers` — list of partition router definitions, each built via `registry.create()`
  - Merge partition dicts from each router into a single dict per combination
  - Purpose: Support multi-dimensional partitioning (e.g., regions x resource_types)
  - _Leverage: `urc/components/partition_router.py`, `urc/registry.py`, `itertools.product`_
  - _Requirements: R1_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec 05-urc-engine-parity, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: Python developer | Task: Add `CartesianProductStreamSlicer` to `partition_router.py`. Constructor takes `stream_slicers` list, builds each via `registry.create()`. `get_partitions(config)` collects partitions from each sub-router, then uses `itertools.product` to generate cross-product, merging dicts. | Restrictions: Handle empty sub-routers gracefully. Safety limit of 100,000 combinations. | Success: 3 lists of [2, 3, 4] values produce 24 partition dicts with all keys present._

## Phase C: Test Infrastructure

- [ ] 6. Set up pytest infrastructure with `responses` library
  - Files: `ucc/urc_app/tests/conftest.py`, `ucc/urc_app/tests/fixtures/mock_apis.py`, `ucc/urc_app/tests/fixtures/sample_manifests.py`, `ucc/urc_app/tests/fixtures/sample_data.py`, `ucc/urc_app/tests/fixtures/__init__.py`
  - Install `responses` and `pytest` as test dependencies
  - Create `conftest.py` with fixtures: `mock_config()`, `mock_checkpoint()`, auto-activate `responses`
  - Create `mock_apis.py` with reusable scenario builders: `register_paginated_api()`, `register_rate_limited_api()`, `register_auth_api()`, `register_bulk_job_api()`, `register_csv_api()`, `register_error_api()`, `register_incremental_api()`
  - Create `sample_manifests.py` with inline YAML strings for each test scenario
  - Create `sample_data.py` with sample records, configs, checkpoint states
  - Purpose: Foundation for all unit and integration tests
  - _Leverage: `responses` library, `pytest`, existing `test_manifests.py` patterns_
  - _Requirements: R2_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec 05-urc-engine-parity, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: Python test engineer | Task: Set up pytest test infrastructure. Install `responses` and `pytest`. Create `conftest.py` with shared fixtures — `mock_config` returns a dict with `base_url`, `api_key`, etc. pointing at a fake URL. `responses_active` auto-activates `responses.RequestsMock` for every test. Create `mock_apis.py` with builder functions that register `responses` callbacks for common patterns (paginated, rate-limited, auth-validating, bulk job, CSV, errors, incremental). Create `sample_manifests.py` with inline YAML manifests. Create `sample_data.py` with sample records and checkpoint states. | Restrictions: All mock URLs must use `https://mock-api.test/` prefix. No real network access. Fixtures must be importable from conftest or fixtures package. | Success: `pytest --co` discovers the test infrastructure, fixtures are importable, `responses` patches `requests` correctly._

## Phase D: Unit Tests

- [ ] 7. Unit tests for interpolation
  - File: `ucc/urc_app/tests/unit/test_interpolation.py`
  - Test `eval_string()`: config vars, nested access, filters (hash, base64, regex), macros (now_utc, timestamp, day_delta, max)
  - Test `eval_dict()`: recursive evaluation, mixed types
  - Test edge cases: undefined var returns original string, non-template passthrough, literal coercion (True/False/None/int/float)
  - Test context vars: response, headers, stream_partition, record
  - Purpose: Validate Jinja2 interpolation engine handles all patterns
  - _Leverage: `urc/interpolation.py`_
  - _Requirements: R2, R4_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec 05-urc-engine-parity, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: Python test engineer | Task: Write comprehensive unit tests for `eval_string()` and `eval_dict()` in `interpolation.py`. Cover: simple config access, nested dict access, all built-in filters (hash, base64encode/decode, regex_search, regex_replace), all macros (now_utc, today_utc, timestamp, max, day_delta), literal coercion, undefined variable fallback, non-string passthrough, additional context variables (response, headers, stream_partition, record). | Restrictions: No network. No mocking needed — pure function tests. | Success: 20+ test cases covering happy paths and edge cases._

- [ ] 8. Unit tests for auth components

  - Test all 8 auth types: NoAuth, ApiKeyAuth, BearerAuth, BasicAuth, OAuth2Auth, DigestAuth, JwtAuth, SessionTokenAuth, SelectiveAuth

  - For JWT: test HS256 signing (PyJWT), token caching, expiry
  - For Selective: test config-based auth selection
  - Purpose: Validate all authentication strategies
  - _Leverage: `urc/components/auth.py`, `responses` library_
  - _Requirements: R2, R4_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec 05-urc-engine-parity, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: Python test engineer | Task: Write unit tests for all auth components. Each test creates the auth instance, calls `apply(session, config)`, and asserts correct headers/params on the session. OAuth2: mock token endpoint via `responses`, assert Bearer header after refresh. JWT: test HS256 with known secret, verify token decodes correctly. SessionToken: mock login endpoint, verify token extraction. Selective: test routing to correct sub-authenticator based on config value. | Restrictions: Use `responses` for any HTTP calls. Mock `time.time()` for expiry tests. | Success: All 8+ auth types tested with both happy path and edge cases (expired token, missing config)._

- [ ] 9. Unit tests for pagination strategies

  - Test: NoPagination, OffsetIncrement, PageIncrement, CursorPagination, DefaultPaginator
  - Test edge cases: empty pages, last page smaller than page_size, cursor from response body vs headers, stop conditions
  - Mock responses with `responses` library for CursorPagination header tests
  - Purpose: Validate all pagination strategies handle boundary conditions
  - _Leverage: `urc/components/pagination.py`, `responses` library_
  - _Requirements: R2, R4_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec 05-urc-engine-parity, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: Python test engineer | Task: Write unit tests for all pagination components. Test `next_token()` for each strategy with mock responses. OffsetIncrement: verify offset advances by record count, stops on short page. PageIncrement: verify page number advances, stops on short page. CursorPagination: test cursor extraction from response body and headers, stop condition evaluation, None/empty cursor. DefaultPaginator: test token injection into params, headers, and RequestPath. NoPagination: always returns None. | Restrictions: Use `responses` for HTTP mocking where needed. Create mock `requests.Response` objects for unit tests. | Success: All strategies tested with normal flow and edge cases (empty page, missing cursor, stop condition true)._

- [ ] 10. Unit tests for decoders (including new CSV/JSONL/ZIP)
  - File: `ucc/urc_app/tests/unit/test_decoders.py`

  - Test XmlDecoder: if present

  - Test JsonlDecoder: normal, empty lines, malformed lines, trailing newline
  - Test ZipfileDecoder: ZIP with JSON files, ZIP with CSV files (inner decoder), empty ZIP

Create mock `requests.Response` objects with `.text`, `.content`, `.json()` set appropriately. CsvDecoder: test normal CSV, BOM-prefixed CSV, custom delimiter/quotechar, malformed rows (assert they're skipped with warning), empty response. JsonlDecoder: test multi-line JSON, empty lines skipped, malformed lines skipped. ZipfileDecoder: create in-memory ZIP files via `zipfile.ZipFile(BytesIO())`, test with JSON and CSV inner content. | Restrictions: No network. Build response mocks manually. | Success: 15+ test cases covering all decoders with happy paths and edge cases._

- [ ] 11. Unit tests for transformations (including new types)
  - File: `ucc/urc_app/tests/unit/test_transformations.py`
  - Test existing: AddFields, RemoveFields, KeysToLower, KeysToSnakeCase, FlattenFields
  - Test new: DpathFlattenFields, KeysReplace, SchemaNormalization

KeysToLower/KeysToSnakeCase: test recursive, nested dicts. FlattenFields: test nested objects, lists. DpathFlattenFields: test specific field extraction, delete_origin. KeysReplace: test multiple replacements, recursive. SchemaNormalization: test special chars, Unicode, leading/trailing underscores. | Restrictions: Pure function tests, no HTTP. | Success: All transform types tested with normal and edge case inputs._

- [ ] 12. Unit tests for error handling and rate limiting
  - File: `ucc/urc_app/tests/unit/test_error_handler.py`, `ucc/urc_app/tests/unit/test_rate_limiter.py`
  - Error handler: test retry logic, backoff strategies (constant, exponential, WaitTimeFromHeader), response filters, CompositeErrorHandler
  - Rate limiter: test TokenBucket (acquire, try_acquire, burst, refill), MovingWindowRateLimiter (window expiry, full window), APIBudget (URL matching, multi-policy)

Test HttpResponseFilter with http_codes, error_message_contains, and predicate. Rate limiters: patch `time.monotonic` to control time. Test TokenBucket: start full, consume all, verify wait_time > 0, advance time, verify refill. Test MovingWindow: fill to capacity, verify blocking, advance past window, verify available. Test APIBudget: URL pattern matching (prefix, wildcard, exact). | Restrictions: MUST mock `time.monotonic()` and `time.sleep()` — zero real delays. | Success: All strategies tested deterministically. Rate limiter tests complete in < 1 second._

  - File: `ucc/urc_app/tests/unit/test_event_timestamp.py`
  - Test CursorBasedTimestamp: auto-derive from incremental_sync, various datetime formats, epoch passthrough
  - Test FieldBasedTimestamp: explicit field, Jinja2 interpolated field/format, missing field fallback
  - Test FetchTimestamp: always returns current time

  - Purpose: Validate Splunk _time resolution for all scenarios

  - _Requirements: R2, R3, R4_

FetchTimestamp: mock `time.time()`, verify it returns mocked value. Test default auto-derivation logic in engine. | Restrictions: Mock `time.time()` for FetchTimestamp.   - File: `ucc/urc_app/tests/unit/test_manifest.py`, `ucc/urc_app/tests/unit/test_registry.py`

Test definitions section is resolved. Use inline YAML strings. | Success: $ref resolution works at 3+ levels, unknown types produce helpful errors._

## Phase E: Integration Tests

  - _Leverage: `urc/engine.py`, `responses` library, `fixtures/mock_apis.py`, `fixtures/sample_manifests.py`_
  - _Requirements: R2, R3, R4_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec 05-urc-engine-parity, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: Python test engineer | Task: Write integration tests that call `collect(manifest_yaml, config)` with `responses`-mocked HTTP. (3) With BearerAuth — verify auth header sent. (4) With AddFields + RemoveFields — verify transformations applied. (5) With rate limiter — verify requests succeed (mock time). Use fixtures from conftest and mock_apis. | Restrictions: All HTTP mocked via `responses`. No real network. - [ ] 18. Integration test: modular input with mocked Splunk SDK
  - File: `ucc/urc_app/tests/integration/test_modular_input.py`
